IS:S(M8-1969 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR EQUIPMENT 
FASTENERS ( WEB EQUIPMENT PATTERN ) 



0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institu- 
tion on 31 March 1969, after the draft finalized by the Fasteners for 
Consumer Goods Sectional Committee had been approved by the Con> 
sumer Products Division Council. 

0.2 The equipment fasteners included in the specification are specially 
suitable for web equipment and similar heavy duty purposes. These 
are mainly used in web equipment of defence personnel, and should, 
therefore, be of reliable construction and be made of non-corrosive 
material. 

0.3 In preparing this standard, assistance has been derived from 
IND/GS/llS Fastener snap» brass, w.e. pattern, issued by the Ministry 
of Defence, Goverment of India. 

0.4 Clause 7.1 of this standard calls for agreement between the pur- 
chaser and the supplier, and permits the purchaser to use his option for 
selection to suit his requirements. 

0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of 
this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, 
expressing the result of a test, shall be -rounded oflfin accordance with 
IS : 2 - I960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded 
off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this 
standard. ""* 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard covers the requirements of equipment fasteners size 
FP52 used in web equipment. 



*Rule« for roundiag o£F namerioal values ( revised )• 

3 



IS : 504K ' 1%9 

2. MATERIAL 

2.1 Tfie equipment fasteners shall be manufactured from the following 
materials: 

a) Components ( other than spring ) — Brass sheet or strip con- 
forming to alloy Designation CuZn37 of IS : 410 - 1967*, and 

b) Spring — Phosphor bronze wire of the following composition and 

strengtli 

Copper 92-& ") 

Tin 70 ^percent 

PhoBphorus 0*2 J 

Tensile strength 94 kgf/mm«, min 

3. SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS 

3.1 The shape and dimensions of different components of web equip- 
ment fastener shall conform to those shown in Fig. I to 3. 

4. MANUFACTURE, WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 

4.1 The equipment fastener shall have two assemblies known as * socket * 
and *8tud* ( see Fig. 4 ). The 'socket* assembly shall consist of 'top 
sub-assembly ' and ' bottom sub-assembly *. The * stud * assembly shall 
consist of *base sub-assembly' and 'washer*. Respective assemblies when 
clenched with a proper assembling tool with the material to be fastened 
shall join together tightly and securely. The two assemblies after being 
put on to the equipment shall have a true fit. 

4.2 The equipment fasteners shall be free from burrs, splits, crack's and 
dents. The top of the top sub-assembly ( Part D, Fig. 3 ) of the fastener 
shall be etched rough resulting in a non-reflecting surface. 

5. TESTS 

5.1 Performtnce Test — The stud and socket assemblies of equipment 
fastener shall be separately clenched on suitable web pieces. The 
fastener shall not show any sign of damage or looseness after opening 
and closing at quick successions in all directions for 500 times. 

5.2 Pall Test — After completing 500 operations as mentioned in 5.1 
the stud and socket assemblies of the fastener shall disengage when a 
load of 10±1 kg is applied gradually.

6. MARKING 

6.1 each equipment fastener shall be clearly stamped with the manu- 
facturer's namci initials or trade-mark. 

6.1.1 Equipment fasteners may also be marked with the ISI Certi- 
fication Mark. 

NOTV — The QM of the 181 Oertlfloation Mark i* governed by the proviatone 
of the Indian Stundarde Institution ( CertiBoation Marks ) Act, and the Ralea and 
Beaulationa made thereunder. Preaenoe of this mark on products covered by an 
Indian Standard conveys the assuranoe that they have been produced to comply 
with the requirements of that standard, under a well-defined system of inspection, 
testing and quality control during production. This system, which is devised and 
supervise^ by 181 and operated by the producer, has the further safeguard that the 
products as actually marketed are continuously checked by ISI for conformity to 
the standard. Details of conditions, under which a licence for the use of the ISI 
Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or prooesaors» may be obtain* 
•d ftom the Indian Standards Institution. 

7. PACKING 

7.1 The equipment fasteners shall be packed in suitable boxes as agreed 
to between the purchaser and the supplier.
